**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN stays constructive on a confirmed fundamental inflection and a confirmed primary trend, but the entry is executed on the neutral analyst's reduced-starter terms rather than the aggressive analyst's 25% at the range ceiling. If no position exists, initiate only 10-15% of a standard allocation near 180.38 (or after a stabilization above the 179.26 low), hold the bulk for the 177.10-178.35 VWMA/10-EMA confluence, and release the final tranche only on a daily close above 181.70 with volume >=45M and a positive MACD histogram. Cap aggregate risk so a close below 171.47 costs no more than ~1.0-1.25% of portfolio value, skip or downsize the 173.30-173.52 shelf, and pause new adds if the 10Y clears 4.34%. If the book already holds AMZN, hold the core and take no add at 180.38.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction is one-sided; sizing is where the debate was actually decided. On fundamentals the bear conceded ("the 10-K is real... I accept the data"): four consecutive quarters of revenue acceleration (9.4% to 10.8% to 12.6% to 13.9%) on a ~$575B base, operating income roughly tripled ($12.2B to $36.9B), record 6.4% operating margin above the 2020 peak, 47.0% gross margin, FCF swing of ~+$49B (-$16.9B to +$32.2B) at 1.06x net income, current ratio 0.94x to 1.05x, cash +36% to $73.4B, liabilities/equity 2.17x to 1.61x. The trend agrees: 180.38 above a rising 10 EMA (178.35), 50 SMA (170.51) and 200 SMA (145.58), ascending March lows 171.47 to 179.26, and a rising VWMA at 177.10. No participant produced any fundamental deterioration, only an entry-timing objection, which earns exposure but not a chase.

The conservative analyst won the two points that govern execution, and the aggressive analyst never refuted them. First, the 25% starter at 180.38 is the weakest-confirmation, widest-stop tranche: ~8.91 points (4.94%, ~2.7 ATR at ATR 3.26) to the 171.47 close-based stop versus only ~5.6-7.6 points to the first objective at 186-188, with the 197.7 measured move underwritable only after the breakout confirms. Buying into the 181.70 ceiling after a 3/28 pierce of the 181.513 upper Bollinger band that closed back inside, with the MACD histogram negative at -0.053, RSI 61.90 diverging from February's 73.78/72.43 peaks, and March turnover at ~34-36M versus 45-50M+ in February, is not clean asymmetry. Second, the 173.30-173.52 add against the same 171.47 stop is ~0.59 ATR away, breaking the plan's own 1xATR rule -- an incoherent risk architecture. The neutral synthesis fixes both: 10-15% starter, aggregate risk 1.0-1.25% of portfolio value instead of 1.5%, skip/downsize that shelf, and a graduated macro guard (add below a 4.10% 10Y, stay small between 4.10-4.34%, pause above 4.34%). The conservative "conditional orders only" stance is too binary: with higher lows 171.47 to 179.26 and price above every key average, a required pullback into 177.10-178.35 with a positive histogram may never fill, and zero exposure through an intact uptrend is its own cost.

Unresolved gaps keep the size smaller, not larger: no market cap, P/E, EV/EBITDA or 52-week range, no insider data, no AWS/advertising segment mix, and a 1-of-3-source sentiment read (Neutral 5.1, low confidence). Sequencing risk is real but not a sell signal -- ~87% of FY2023 FCF landed in Q4, so weak Q1-Q3'24 FCF prints are expected seasonality; only weakness plus commentary that the concentration was not seasonal changes the thesis. The -17.2% capex cut to $52.7B, the non-repeatability of 400bps of margin expansion, and H2'24 lapping 7.8% operating-margin comps cap the rate of upside, not the direction. Thesis-changers: a failed breakout (rejection at 181.70 on >=45M volume closing below 177.10), a decisive 10Y move above 4.34%, a Q1'24 FCF miss with non-seasonal commentary, arrival of valuation data showing a clear premium to AMZN's own history without matching earnings revisions, or a close below 165.74, the post-gap February low, which invalidates the full position.

**Price Target**: 186.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months
